text:
mike: Heads up — seeing p95/p99 climb on text-gen in us-west2 over the last 20m. Correlates with high queue depth on the serving pool.

sara: graph? link?

mike: https://grafana.redwood/shot/abcd1234 p95 ~220ms -> 420ms, p99 ~1.1s. Batcher logs show sustained fills at max_batch and many small requests waiting for packing.

kevin: ops-bot alerted earlier:
ops-bot: ALERT batcher_queue_depth gpu-pool-usw2-3 > 300 for 12m; admission_denied=4.2%

jess: Is this the adaptive-batcher change we rolled yesterday (pack-window=20ms -> 50ms)?

mike: yup. Pack window increase makes the batcher wait longer to build fuller batches. Works great for throughput but we started hitting latency SLOs for low-seq jobs.

sara: Could be two issues combined: pack window up + noisy tenant creating single-token bursts. Those bursts inflate avg fill but push latency for others.

kevin: Quick mitigation: reduce pack-window to 30ms or lower max_batch for that shard. Tradeoff is throughput. We can also tighten admission so latency-critical routes bypass packing.

luis-oncall: I can patch config on the pool for a canary shard. Prefer changing pack-window first, less impactful on cost.

jess: +1. Let's do a canary: change pool gpu-pool-usw2-3 -> pack_window=25ms, max_batch keep at 128 for now. Roll to 2 nodes, monitor 15m.

kevin: To be explicit, proposed steps:
1) oncall patch `pool.cfg` for shard 3: `pack_window_ms = 25`
2) set alert threshold p99 > 600ms -> auto rollback to previous config
3) route a small percentage (5%) of latency-critical traffic to dedicated low-latency path (no packing)

mike: also add a short-term admission tweak: prefer oldest-first scheduling to reduce head-of-line wait for tiny requests.

sara: FYI this will increase per-token cost for the low-latency path, call it out in the change message.

luis-oncall: applying canary now to gpu-pool-usw2-3 node ids [n-117, n-118].

ops-bot: DEPLOY START canary-config-update by luis-oncall at 1835567865
ops-bot: DEPLOY DONE canary-config-update success on [n-117]

mike: early numbers: p95 down to 240ms on canary node, p99 down to 480ms. Queue depth dropped ~45%.

jess: good. If stable for 15m, roll to remaining nodes in the pool. Coordinate with cost team before widening the dedicated no-pack path.

kevin: Long term we should add tenant-aware admission: latency-tagged requests get preference and smaller max_batch, while batch-friendly tenants are aggregated more aggressively.

sara: filing a follow-up: https://tickets.redwood/INF-4321 "Tenant-aware admission + pack window autoscaler". Assigning to kevin + eng-runtime.

luis-oncall: rolling to rest of pool in 2m.

ops-bot: DEPLOY START canary-config-rollout by luis-oncall at 1835567920
ops-bot: DEPLOY DONE rollout success on [n-118, n-119, n-120]

mike: after full pool change p95 ~230ms, p99 ~500ms. Still above baseline but acceptable. We'll treat this as a temporary config until we implement smarter admission.

jess: thanks everyone. Action items: kevin to design tenant-aware admission (ETA 2w), sara to coordinate cost impact doc, mike to watch SLOs for 24h.

sara: :thumbsup:

mike: tagging @oncall-rotation for follow-up if things regress.
